To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

Orchestia grillis, a detritivorous amphibod, feeds upon microorganisms associated with Spartina litter, but not upon the litter itself; microorganisms respond to Orcestia grazing by increasing metabolic activity, reflected by increased decomposition of nitrogen in litter and increased microbial growth; increased microbial activity is a direct response of microorganisms to grazing, and not an indirect response mediated by Orchestia excretion of ammonia or increased diffusion rates; increased microbial growth is a result of increased availability of nitrogen

Orchestia efficiently feeds on microorganisms attached to Spartina litter, that this grazing increases microbial metabolic activity, and that this increase is due to both ammonia excretion and increased diffusion rates and to direct grazing.

the detritivorous amphipod Orchestia grillis feeds on microorganisms attached to Spartina litter, and that the microbial community responds to grazing by increasing its metabolic activity, reflected primarily in increased microbial biomass.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of detritivores on detritus.
the role of detritivores in the decomposition of Spartina alternifloralitter in the salt marshes of the Georgia coast.
the effects of grazing by the amphipod Orchestia grillusi on Spartina litter decomposition.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Orchestia is a detritivore which grazes on microorganisms associated with Spartina litter, and that this grazing activity increases microbial activity and decomposition rate of the litter.
Orchestia grazing increases litter decomposition by stimulating microbial growth.
Orchestia grazing increases microbial activity and biomass and accelerates litter decomposition.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

Orchestia is a major consumer of the microbial community attached to Spartina litter, and the effect of grazing is to increase the rate of decomposition of the nitrogenous fraction of litter, and the rate of growth of microorganisms attached to litter.
the detritivorous amphipod Orchestia grillis has a significant impact on the microbial community attached to Spartina litter and the associated decomposition processes.

Orchestia is an efficient detritivore that does not directly digest Spartina litter, but rather feeds upon microorganisms associated with litter, and in doing so, accelerates decomposition and increases microbial activity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the effect of detritivores on microbial community structure and functioning can be profound and may not be easily predicted from simple measures of grazing pressure.
the detritivores can have a significant effect on the decomposition of litter, and that this effect is mediated through the microbial community associated with the litter.
detritivores are not simply “waste disposal” organisms, but are important components of food webs.
